summary: Generic agent step executions retain claim-backed historical metadata and exact retry usage

replay.detail: Execution envelopes read durable work claims and replicated response rollups, not trimmed local timelines. Historical claims without declaration, trace or invocation accounting evidence keep unknown metadata; earlier aggregate spend is never guessed onto an invocation. Pre-claim startup failures remain independent runtime/readiness evidence.

schema.detail: Adds optional declared_model, trace_id and fallback work-claim fields, optional execution_id on response rollups, and a local exact-invocation spend partition. The response-rollup retention and period-series keys include execution_id. Existing aggregate tables and series remain readable and unchanged.

rules.detail: Response-source deduplication and generic reported-cost/list-price accounting are unchanged. Exact attribution requires one unambiguous durable work claim with an unexpired historical lease for the agent incarnation at response time; missing expiry and future renewals cannot establish ownership. Retries and reclaims have distinct claim-ID accounting keys. Final rollup totals retain each execution partition through compaction.

compatibility.detail: The kernel exports Serialize/Deserialize StepExecution and StepExecutionUsage, and Store exposes step_executions. New claims capture the declared model and only an actual valid propagated OpenTelemetry trace. Model drift does not imply fallback, absent usage is null, and unpriced tokens remain explicit. The earliest applicable native exit bounds duration even when later cleanup closes the step. Older fleets still retain the optional-field claims; readers that do not include execution_id in rollup keys must be upgraded before relying on exact per-attempt totals.

downtime.detail: No forced seat restart or historical usage rewrite. A new derived period index is created on open.

manual.detail: No manual migration. See historical step executions in the model-account documentation.

recovery.detail: Retain the database and immutable claim log during rollback. An older reader does not distinguish execution partitions and cannot provide exact retry accounting; upgrade readers again to recover the claim-backed view.
